note: a + el → al, de + el → del (vamos al centro, el carro del hotel). Feminine nouns starting with a stressed a- take el: el agua fría. Él with an accent = he.
No contraction with a/de: a la playa, de la casa. Also an object pronoun (her/it) — see la (pronoun).
de + el = del (el centro del pueblo). Possession: el carro de Ana = Ana's car. Material/kind: taco de pastor. Before a vowel it glides into the next word.
No accent = that/which/who: el taco que pedí, dice que viene. Comparisons: más que (more than). lo que = what (the thing that). ¿qué? with accent = what? Also starts wishes: ¡que te vaya bien!

ex_es: Tacos y una coca, por favor.
note: Becomes e before a word starting with the sound i (i-, hi-): padre e hijo. Telling time: las dos y media (2:30). ¿Y tú? = and you?
a + el = al (voy al mercado). Time: a las tres (at three). Personal a before people as objects: veo a María. ir a + infinitive = going to: voy a comer.
One word for in/on/at: en la mesa (on the table), en casa (at home), en el centro (downtown). Transport: en camión, en metro, en taxi (but a pie = on foot).
Mixed groups take the masculine: los niños = the kids (boys and girls). Also an object pronoun (them) — see los (pronoun).
uno shortens to un before a masculine noun: un peso, veintiún pesos. Spanish leaves it out with jobs: soy maestro (I'm a teacher).
Many jobs: reflexive (se llama Ana), impersonal (se vende = for sale; ¿cómo se dice...? = how do you say...?), and replacing le/les before lo/la (se lo doy). Not sé (I know).
Goes before the verb and any object pronouns: no lo sé. Double negatives are normal and required: no hay nada, no viene nadie. Tag question: ¿no? = right?

ex_es: Un café con leche, por favor.
note: con + mí = conmigo, con + ti = contigo. Con permiso = excuse me (passing by). Con gusto = with pleasure / you're welcome (very Mexican).

en: for, because of, through, by, per, in exchange for
note: por vs para: por = cause (gracias por, por eso), route (por aquí, por el parque), exchange (por cien pesos), time of day (por la mañana), means (por teléfono), per (cien por ciento). para = goal/destination/recipient/deadline.

ex_en: Can I have your name, please?
note: Very ambiguous: su casa can be his, her, their or your (formal) house. Context or de él / de usted clarifies.

ex_es: Una mesa para dos, por favor.
note: un/una also mean 'one': una cerveza = one beer. Before stressed a-: un agua (but una agua is heard in Mexico).
Used for time: a las tres = at three o'clock (las horas).

en: for; in order to (purpose, destination, deadline, recipient)
note: por vs para: para = purpose (para comer), destination (para el centro), recipient (para ti), deadline (para el lunes), opinion (para mí). por = cause, route, exchange, duration. para que + subjunctive = so that. In speech para is almost always pa'.

en: him, it (masculine direct object); the ... thing (neuter)
note: le vs lo: lo = direct object (lo veo = I see him/it); le = indirect (le digo = I tell him/her/you). Mexico says lo veo for 'I see him', not Spain's le veo. Neuter: lo bueno = the good thing; lo que = what.

ex_en: Shall I bring you the check?
note: Indirect object (to/for someone). Before lo/la/los/las it becomes se: se lo doy (I give it to him). Mexico adds a playful le to many words: ándale, órale, híjole, córrele.

No accent = like/as/since/about: como a las tres (around three), como no tengo carro... (since I don't have a car...). ¿cómo? with accent = how? Mexico uses como + adjective as a filler: está como caro (it's kind of pricey).
más... que = more than; el más grande = the biggest; ¿algo más? = anything else?; nada más = that's all. Math: dos más dos.
pero vs sino: after a negative, use sino to correct the first idea (no es caro sino barato); pero adds a contrast (no es caro, pero no me gusta).

ex_en: Can I have a coffee, please?
note: Goes before a conjugated verb (me gusta, me llamo) and attaches to infinitives, gerunds and commands (quiero verte, dame). ¿Me da...? is the standard Mexican way to order.

ex_en: What do you want to eat?
note: qué vs cuál: qué + noun (¿qué color?) and to ask for a definition (¿qué es esto?); cuál before ser to pick specific info (¿cuál es tu nombre?). ¡Qué bonito! = how pretty! A bare ¿qué? to ask for a repeat is blunt — Mexicans say ¿mande?
todo el día = all day; todos los días = every day; todo = everything. ¿Todo bien? is a standard greeting check.
Never 'un otro': otro café = another coffee. Otra vez = again. ¡Otra! = encore!

en: already; now; (ya no) anymore; right away
note: ya no = not anymore (ya no hay = there's none left); ¡ya voy! = coming!; ya mero = almost (Mexico); ya sé = I know. Often just adds 'now/finally': ya está listo.
Becomes u before o- / ho-: siete u ocho. Between numerals sometimes written ó (old rule). o sea = I mean.
No accent = if; sí with accent = yes. Si + present for real conditions: si llueve, no voy. Starts soft protests: ¡si ya te dije! (but I already told you!).
Object form of tú: te quiero, te veo. Formal equivalent: lo/la/le (lo veo, le digo). Not té (tea).
Forms: este, esta, estos, estas (neuter esto). este/ese/aquel = this / that (near you) / that over there. Also Mexico's number-one filler: este... = um..., which you'll hear constantly.
No accent (mí = me). Plural mis: mis amigos. In speech mi hijo/mi hija often merge to mijo/mija, a common term of affection in Mexico.
Usually dropped because the verb shows the person (quiero = I want); say yo for contrast or emphasis: yo pago (I'll pay).
Neuter. ¡Eso! = that's it! / way to go! Por eso = that's why. Eso sí = that, yes / admittedly.

en: her, it (feminine direct object); you (formal, to a woman)
ex_en: The key? I don't have it.
note: Direct object only: la veo (I see her). 'To her' is le: le digo (I tell her).
Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas (neuter eso). ese = near the listener or just mentioned; aquel = far from both. Mexico slang: ¡ése! = hey, buddy.

ex_en: I'm not going because I'm tired.
note: porque (one word, no accent) = because; ¿por qué? (two words, accent) = why? A complete answer to ¿por qué? starts with porque.
Only before adjectives and adverbs: muy caro, muy bien. Never alone and never before nouns: —¿Te gusta? —Sí, mucho (not 'sí, muy').

ex_en: When you arrive, let me know.
note: No accent outside questions; ¿cuándo? = when? For a future event it takes the subjunctive: cuando llegues (not cuando llegarás).

en: on, on top of; about; over
ex_es: Las llaves están sobre la mesa.
ex_en: The keys are on the table.
note: Also 'about': un libro sobre México. sobre todo = above all, especially. sobre vs en: en la mesa is more common in speech.
bien vs bueno: bien is the adverb (está bien, cantas bien), bueno the adjective (un buen libro). Mexico uses bien = very: bien rico, bien lejos. ¿Está bien? = is that OK?
Shortens to algún before a masculine singular noun: algún día (someday). alguno = some vs ninguno = none.
Accent = yes; si without accent = if. Emphasis: sí quiero (I DO want). ¡Claro que sí! = of course!
el mismo día = the same day; yo mismo = myself; ahora mismo / aquí mismo = right now / right here; lo mismo = the same thing. Position matters: el presidente mismo = the president himself.

en: a lot of, much, many; (adverb) a lot
ex_en: There's a lot of traffic today.
note: muy vs mucho: muy + adjective/adverb (muy caro), mucho + noun or after a verb (mucho calor, trabajo mucho). Never 'muy mucho'. Muchas gracias!
Huge filler in Mexico: pues sí (well, yes), pues no (well, no), ándale pues (OK then). At the end it adds insistence: ¡ya, pues! (come on, enough!). Rural/fast speech: pos, ps.
aquí vs acá: both mean here; Mexico uses both, acá a bit more for 'over here' with motion (ven acá). Por aquí = around here / this way.

ex_es: Dos tacos de pastor, por favor.

en: us, to us, ourselves, each other
note: nos vemos = see you (literally 'we see each other') — the everyday goodbye.
The accent separates él (he) from el (the). After prepositions: para él, con él.

tú vs usted: tú with friends, kids, people your age; usted with strangers, elders, police, service staff. In Mexico usted is the safe default; switch when they tutean you. tú (you) has an accent; tu (your) does not.

en: like this, like that, this way; so
note: ¿Así? = like this?; así es = that's right; así que = so; así así = so-so; así nomás = just like that.

ex_es: Es mi primera vez en México.
ex_en: It's my first time in Mexico.
note: Shortens to primer before a masculine singular noun: el primer piso. Dates: el primero de mayo (Mexico doesn't say el uno). As adverb: primero comemos (first we eat).
Opposite in negative sentences: tampoco (me neither).
desde... hasta = from... to (desde aquí hasta el Zócalo). desde hace = for (time up to now): desde hace dos años.

en: this (thing, idea — no noun after it)
note: Neuter: for things you don't name. Never esto libro — say este libro.

en: big, large; great (before a noun: gran)
note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun, and the meaning shifts: un gran hombre = a great man; un hombre grande = a big man. Mexico: ya está grande = he's grown up / getting old.

en: nor, not even; (ni... ni) neither... nor
note: ni... ni = neither... nor: ni frío ni calor. ¡Ni modo! = oh well, nothing to be done (extremely Mexican). Ni siquiera = not even.

ex_es: Un café sin azúcar, por favor.
note: sin + infinitive: sin comer (without eating). Sin embargo = however.

en: until, up to, as far as; even
note: Time: hasta las diez (until ten). Place: hasta la esquina (as far as the corner). 'Even': hasta los niños saben. Hasta luego = see you later.

ex_en: So, are we going or not?
note: Both 'at that time' (en ese entonces) and the conversational 'so...'. Very common filler; heavily reduced in fast speech.
No accent; tú with an accent = you. Formal 'your' is su.

ex_es: Está entre el banco y la farmacia.
ex_en: It's between the bank and the pharmacy.
note: entre tú y yo = between you and me (not entre ti y mí). entre semana = on weekdays.
uno → un before a masculine noun (un taco, veintiún pesos); una before a feminine one. Also 'one/you' in general statements: uno nunca sabe.
After prepositions too: con ella, para ella.
Double negative is required: no veo nada (I don't see anything). De nada = you're welcome. Nada más = only / that's all.
Takes the él/ella verb form: usted habla, usted es. Written Ud. or Ud. Mexicans use it a lot, even with family in some regions.

Shortens to buen before a masculine singular noun: buen día, buen provecho. bueno vs bien: bueno describes nouns, bien modifies verbs (es bueno / está bien). The phone/filler bueno is a separate entry.

en: so much, so many; as much
note: tanto + noun, tan + adjective: tanto tráfico / tan caro. tanto como = as much as. Por lo tanto = therefore.

ex_en: Do you want something to drink?
note: algo + adjective = somewhat: algo caro (kind of expensive). ¿Algo más? = anything else?
¿Cómo? = sorry, what? (Mexicans prefer ¿mande?). ¡Cómo no! = of course! ¿Cómo te llamas? = what's your name?

ex_es: Nuestro hotel está en el centro.
note: Agrees with the noun owned: nuestra casa, nuestros amigos.

en: so, as (before an adjective or adverb)
note: tan + adj + como = as... as: tan grande como. tan vs tanto: tan before adjectives/adverbs, tanto with nouns and verbs.

en: them (masculine or mixed object); you all
ex_en: I'll wait for you all outside.
note: Direct object: los veo (I see them / I see you all). 'To them' is les.

ex_en: And now what do we do?
note: ahora mismo = right now. Ahora que = now that. In Mexico ora is the casual form: ¡ora sí! (now we're talking!).

en: little, few, not much; (un poco) a bit
note: un poco = a little (positive): un poco de agua. poco = not much (negative): habla poco. Mexico loves the diminutive: un poquito.

ex_en: It's the house where I live.
note: No accent outside questions. En donde is common in Mexico. Mexico also uses donde = if: donde no vengas... (if you don't come...).
Mexico: siempre sí / siempre no = 'it turns out yes/no after all' (siempre no voy = I'm not going after all).
ellas = they (all female). Mixed groups use ellos.
Never changes form. cada uno = each one; cada vez más = more and more.
por lo menos = at least; menos mal = thank goodness. Time: las tres menos cuarto (Mexico says un cuarto para las tres).
Position: un carro nuevo = a brand-new car; un nuevo carro = a different car (new to me). De nuevo = again. Año Nuevo = New Year.
Adjective = alone (estoy sola, viajan solos). The adverb solo = only is a separate entry. A solas = in private.
Older spelling sólo (with accent) for 'only'; current rules drop the accent. Solo is also an adjective = alone (estoy solo).
Indirect object plural. Becomes se before lo/la: se lo doy (I give it to them).
Two words + accent = why?; porque (one word) = because; el porqué = the reason.

en: well...; OK; hello? (answering the phone in Mexico)
note: Mexico answers the phone with ¿Bueno? (Spain: ¿Diga?). As a filler: bueno, ya me voy (well, I'm off). Bueno vs bien: bueno is the adjective, bien the adverb.

ex_en: Afterwards we'll go to the market.
note: después de + noun or infinitive: después de comer (after eating). Hasta después = see you later.
Comparative of bueno/bien (not más bueno): mejor que = better than; el/la mejor = the best. Also an adverb: canta mejor. A lo mejor = maybe (very Mexican).
nosotras = we (all women). Verb ends in -mos: vamos, somos, comemos.
Before the verb alone (nunca voy) or after it with no (no voy nunca). Casi nunca = hardly ever.

ex_en: I used to live in Monterrey.
note: antes de + noun/infinitive: antes de las ocho, antes de salir. Cuanto antes = as soon as possible.
With motion: ¿a dónde vas? (also written adónde). Origin: ¿de dónde eres? = where are you from? Accent only in questions.
hoy en día = nowadays. ¿Qué día es hoy? = what's today's date/day?
unos/unas + number = approximately: unas tres horas (about three hours).

ex_en: Even if it rains, we're going.
note: Indicative = although (fact): aunque llueve. Subjunctive = even if (maybe): aunque llueva.
mayor = older (hermano mayor), elderly (una señora mayor — the polite word, not vieja), bigger (la mayor parte = most). Al por mayor = wholesale. Mayor de edad = adult (18+).
Plural quiénes for groups: ¿quiénes vienen? ¿De quién es? = whose is it? Accent only in questions/exclamations.
ahí (near you / just there), allá (over there, far). Mexico uses ahí much more than allí. Ahí nos vemos = see you around. In fast speech the two vowels merge into one syllable.
Mexico: luego luego = right away, immediately; desde luego = of course; hasta luego = see you later. Luego can also mean 'sometimes' in Mexico: luego no hay agua.
la última vez = the last time; lo último = the latest thing. Por último = lastly. A última hora = at the last minute.

en: true; certain, sure; (before a noun) a certain
note: Position: es cierto = it's true; cierta persona = a certain person (no un before it). Por cierto = by the way.

ex_en: Do you all want anything else?
note: In Mexico ustedes is the only plural 'you', for friends and strangers alike. Spain's vosotros is not used. Takes the ellos verb form: ustedes hablan.
Before the noun = own (mi propio cuarto); after = typical / appropriate (propio de México).
además de = in addition to: además de caro, es feo.
por lo general / en general = generally. Noun el general = an army general.
Mexican speech prefers chico / chiquito; pequeño sounds a bit more careful. Los pequeños = the little ones.

ex_en: He's the one who helped me.
note: No accent outside questions. Plural quienes. Speech often uses que or el que instead.

ex_es: Una mesa para cuatro, por favor.

note: Speech often uses por or nothing: viví ahí (por) dos años.
Mexico also says ya mero. Casi nunca = hardly ever.
With an accent = me after prepositions (para mí, a mí me gusta). con + mí = conmigo. mi without accent = my.

ex_es: No hay nadie en la casa.
note: Double negative: no viene nadie. Before the verb alone: nadie sabe.

ex_en: Is there a public bathroom nearby?
note: el público = the audience / the public. Transporte público = public transportation.
Opposite: nadie. Takes the personal a: ¿viste a alguien?
Lo importante es... = the important thing is...
mañana = tomorrow; la mañana = the morning (separate entry); mañana en la mañana = tomorrow morning; pasado mañana = the day after tomorrow.
mientras tanto = meanwhile. mientras que = whereas.
Never 'un mil': mil = 1,000, dos mil = 2,000. Doesn't take -s: tres mil. Miles = thousands (miles de personas). Mexico writes 1,000 with a comma like the US.

ex_en: I don't talk about political topics.
Thank you very much, very kind.
note: Replies: de nada, con gusto, a la orden (Mexico, from shop and service staff), no hay de qué.

ex_en: The tortillas? I already bought them.
note: Direct object for feminine plural nouns. 'To them' is les.

ex_en: I saw it on social media.
Is it possible to pay by card?
note: lo más pronto posible = as soon as possible.
Pain (¡ay!), surprise, emotion, complaint. ¡Ay, no! = oh no! Sounds like hay (there is) but spelled differently.

ex_es: Le dejo cinco pesos de propina.
ex_en: I'll leave you a five-peso tip.

note: Also a noun: un segundo (a second). ¡Un segundo! = just a sec!
en voz alta = out loud. ¡Alto! = stop (Mexican stop signs say ALTO). Before the noun: un alto funcionario = a high-ranking official.
qué vs cuál: use cuál with ser for specific info (¿cuál es tu dirección?, not ¿qué es...?) and to choose among options (¿cuál quieres?).
mal (adverb) vs malo (adjective): está mal (it's wrong) vs es malo (it's bad). mal is also the short form of malo before a masculine noun: un mal día.

Adjective before the noun with no un: medio kilo, media hora. As an adverb it doesn't change: está medio cansada (she's kind of tired). medio vs mitad: medio describes (media naranja), la mitad is the noun (la mitad del pastel).
Shortens to ningún before a masculine singular noun. Almost always singular: no tengo ninguna duda. Needs no before the verb if it comes after.
todavía no = not yet; aún means the same. Fast speech drops the d.

Position: un viejo amigo = a long-time friend; un amigo viejo = an elderly friend. For people, viejo can sound rude — say mayor. Mexico: mi viejo / mi vieja = my dad/mom or my husband/wife (affectionate).
Colors: azul claro, verde claro (claro doesn't agree there). Está claro = it's clear. Interjection ¡claro! (of course) is a separate entry.
Accent only in questions; cuando (no accent) = when (statement). ¿Desde cuándo? = since when?
hacia las cinco = around five. hacia vs para: hacia = direction only; para = destination.
Plural adds an accent: jóvenes. ¡Joven! is how you call a young waiter or shop assistant in Mexico (señorita for women).
Shortens to mal before a masculine singular noun: un mal día. ser malo = bad / mean; estar malo = sick (Mexico) or gone bad (food). Mala onda = not cool / mean.
¿Qué tal? = how's it going? / how was it?; tal vez = maybe; un tal Juan = some guy called Juan; con tal de que = as long as.
Agrees: juntos, juntas. junto a = next to; junto con = together with.
Also 'back there / in that place': allá en Texas. Para allá = that way (pa'llá). Más allá = further on.
False friend: largo = long, NOT large (= grande). A lo largo de = along.
Vuelo nacional = domestic flight (Mexico). Salidas nacionales = domestic departures.
For skin, moreno is the polite everyday word. Mercado negro = black market.
Arroz blanco is a standard side. En blanco = blank.
antier (Mexico) = the day before yesterday.

ex_es: Es una pastilla contra el dolor.
note: en contra de = against (an idea). Mexico: contra is used for medicine 'for': algo contra la diarrea.
Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántas tortillas? ¿cuántos años tienes? ¿Cuánto es? = how much is it (all)? ¿Cuánto le debo? = what do I owe you?
Me da igual = I don't mind. Mexico: igual y... = maybe (igual y llueve); igual = anyway (igual voy). Igual que = the same as.
Also 'royal' (Camino Real). 'Actually' = en realidad.

ex_es: No es mío, sino de Ana.
note: Only after a negative, replacing the first idea. Before a clause: sino que (no lo compré sino que me lo regalaron).

ex_es: Es el único hotel del pueblo.
ex_en: It's the only hotel in town.
note: Position: hijo único = only child; la única vez = the only time; es único = it's one of a kind.
ser humano = human being; derechos humanos = human rights.
cerca de = near to: cerca del hotel. Mexican diminutive: cerquita (really close).
Fine everywhere in Mexico. In shops and with strangers add buenos días / buenas tardes / buenas noches — Mexicans often greet with just ¡buenas!
Synonyms: hasta, aun.
Works like a noun: un millón, dos millones, and takes de before a noun (un millón de personas).

ex_en: Is it safe to walk at night?
note: ser seguro = safe; estar seguro = sure. ¡Seguro! = sure!; seguro que sí = surely. The noun el seguro = insurance.

ex_en: Get off at the next stop.
note: ¡El siguiente! = next (in line)! Al día siguiente = the next day.
Tag question added to the end, like ¿no?. The noun la verdad = the truth. Mexicans very often drop the final d.

ex_en: I'm looking for an inexpensive hotel.
note: The polite word for 'cheap': ¿tiene algo más económico? (barato is fine too).
With accent = still/yet (= todavía). aun without accent = even (aun así = even so).

en: which (in el cual, la cual — formal relative)
ex_es: Es la calle en la cual vivo.
ex_en: It's the street I live on.
note: Always with an article as a relative: el cual, la cual, lo cual (which = that whole idea). Speech prefers que / donde.

ex_es: El español no es tan difícil.

note: Never takes an accent. con + ti = contigo. a ti te gusta = YOU like it.
Opposite of alto. Planta baja = ground floor (PB in elevators). The preposition bajo (under) is a separate entry. Mexico: bajito = shortish, or 'quietly'.
Plato fuerte = main course. Hablar fuerte = to speak loudly. Lluvia fuerte = heavy rain.

en: quite a lot, enough; (adverb) quite, rather
note: Means 'quite/rather' more often than 'enough'. With nouns: bastante comida (plenty of food).
Before a noun; alone it's cualquiera (cualquiera sirve = any one will do). Shortened form, like buen and gran.
Only before the i sound: e hijos, e Isabel; but y hielo (sounds 'ye').
fuera de = outside of. ¡Fuera! = out! Mexico usually says afuera on its own.
lejos de = far from: lejos de aquí.
Adverb 'late' (llegar tarde). The noun la tarde = afternoon/evening (buenas tardes) is a separate entry. Más tarde = later.
Lo necesario = what's needed. Si es necesario = if necessary.
Very common in Mexico, especially with motion. Para acá = this way (pa'cá in speech).
Position: un hombre pobre = a man with no money; ¡pobre hombre! = poor guy (pitiable). ¡Pobrecito! = poor thing!

ex_es: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
ex_en: It's expensive; however, it's worth it.
note: More formal; speech often uses pero or aun así.
'Me neither' = yo tampoco, never 'yo también no'. After the verb add no: no lo sé tampoco.
libre = free/unoccupied (taxi libre, día libre). 'Free of charge' is gratis. Lucha libre = Mexican masked wrestling. Al aire libre = outdoors.

ex_es: Según el mapa, es por aquí.
ex_en: According to the map, it's this way.
note: Alone as an answer: —¿Vas? —Según. = It depends. Takes subject pronouns: según tú.
En especial = especially.
Plato principal = main course.

ex_en: My grandma used to live there.
note: Less common in Mexican speech than ahí and allá.
Two senses: 'barely' (apenas alcanza) and 'just now / only just' (apenas llegué = I just got here).
cien alone or before a noun or mil/millones (cien pesos, cien mil); ciento when more follows (ciento veinte). Never 'un cien'. Percent: por ciento.
¡Claro que sí! = of course! ¡Claro que no! = of course not! Also ¡cómo no! (very common in Mexico).
Plural felices. ser feliz (a happy person) and estar feliz (happy now) are both used. ¡Feliz viaje! = have a good trip. Felices fiestas.
menor de edad = a minor (under 18). For size speech prefers más chico.
Día de Muertos = Day of the Dead (Nov 1–2). muerto de hambre = starving; muerto de risa = dying of laughter.

en: I mean, in other words, that is
ex_en: So you mean you're not coming?
note: Clarifier and filler; very heavy use in Mexico City youth (fresa) speech: o sea, como que, ¿no?

ex_es: La semana pasada fui a Puebla.
ex_en: Last week I went to Puebla.
note: el año pasado = last year; el pasado = the past; pasado mañana = the day after tomorrow.
de pronto = suddenly; lo más pronto posible = as soon as possible.
Same as quizás. Spelled as two words (talvez is a common misspelling).
Always plural. Means 'several', not 'various kinds' (that's diversos).

ex_es: El costo total es de mil pesos.
ex_en: The total cost is a thousand pesos.
note: en total = in total. Mexico: total que... = anyway, long story short...
False friend: actual = current, not 'actual' (= real / verdadero). Actualmente = currently.
Before a plural noun = various: diferentes lugares.

en: that (over there, far away; long ago)
ex_en: Do you see that building over there?
note: Forms: aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas. Also distant time: en aquellos años (back in those years). Speech often uses ese instead.
¡Arriba México! = go, Mexico! Para arriba = upward. Calle arriba = up the street.
atrás = behind (often with motion); detrás de = behind (a thing). Para atrás = backwards. Años atrás = years ago.
